note: Synthetic memories for the retrieval benchmark. Written for it; no real user's memories. The session's project is github.com/example/ledger; github.com/example/website must never be returned.

memories.title: Keep pull requests under 400 changed lines
memories.content: Split work so that each pull request changes fewer than 400 lines; reviewers lose focus on larger diffs and approve what they did not read.

memories.title: Rebase feature branches onto main instead of merging main into them
memories.content: Bring a feature branch up to date by rebasing it onto main, never by merging main into it, so the log reads as one straight line of changes.

memories.title: Post a daily status note in the team channel before 10:00
memories.content: Every working day, post a short status note in the team channel before 10:00: what was done, what is next, what blocks.

memories.title: Start every branch name with the tracker ticket, like feat/ENG-123-short-name
memories.content: Branch names carry the tracker ticket after the type, such as feat/ENG-123-short-name or fix/ENG-88-login-timeout, so the tracker links them.

memories.title: No production deploys on Fridays after 15:00
memories.content: Do not deploy to production on a Friday after 15:00 local time; anything that breaks then waits for the weekend's skeleton crew.

memories.title: Merge only after one approving review, even for small fixes
memories.content: Every change needs one approving review before it is merged, typo fixes included; no self-merges.

memories.title: Add user-visible changes under Unreleased in CHANGELOG.md
memories.content: Each change a user can notice gets a line under the Unreleased heading of CHANGELOG.md in the same pull request.

memories.title: Open pull requests as drafts until CI passes
memories.content: Open a pull request as a draft and mark it ready only once continuous integration is green, so nobody reviews a broken build.

memories.title: Hotfixes branch from the release tag, then get cherry-picked to main
memories.content: An urgent fix for a shipped version branches from that version's tag, ships as a patch, and is then cherry-picked onto main.

memories.title: Decline meetings that have no agenda
memories.content: The user declines meeting invitations that come without an agenda; propose one before inviting them.

memories.title: Wrap Go errors with %w and a short context
memories.content: In Go, return errors wrapped with fmt.Errorf and %w plus a few words of context, such as "load config: %w", so callers can unwrap them.

memories.title: Library code returns errors and never calls panic or exit
memories.content: Code in a library hands every failure back to its caller as an error value; it never panics or exits the process, which only an application may decide.

memories.title: TypeScript projects use strict mode with no implicit any
memories.content: Enable strict in tsconfig.json and keep noImplicitAny on; give unknown values the unknown type instead of any.

memories.title: Type-annotate public Python functions and check with mypy --strict
memories.content: Every public Python function carries type annotations, and the code passes mypy --strict before it is merged.

memories.title: Always use parameterized SQL; never format values into a query string
memories.content: Pass values to SQL through bound parameters; building a query by formatting or concatenating values into its text is never allowed.

memories.title: Keep functions under 40 lines and extract helpers when longer
memories.content: A function longer than about 40 lines gets split into named helpers so each part can be read on one screen.

memories.title: Name booleans as questions, like isReady or hasAccess
memories.content: Boolean variables and fields read as yes-or-no questions: isReady, hasAccess, canRetry.

memories.title: Store timestamps in UTC and convert to local time only for display
memories.content: Every stored date and time is in UTC; conversion to the reader's zone happens only where it is shown.

memories.title: Guard unfinished features behind flags and remove each flag within two releases
memories.content: Work that is merged before it is finished stays behind a feature flag, off by default, and the flag is deleted no later than two releases after the feature ships.

memories.title: Log structured JSON with a request id on every line
memories.content: Services write logs as one JSON object per line, each carrying the request_id of the call it belongs to.

memories.title: Pin direct dependencies exactly and review upgrades weekly
memories.content: Direct dependencies are pinned to exact versions in the lock file; a weekly pass reviews and applies upgrades.

memories.title: Prefer immutable data structures for shared state
memories.content: State shared between threads or components is held in immutable structures that are replaced, not mutated in place.

memories.title: Quarantine a flaky test within a day and file a ticket for it
memories.content: A test that passes and fails without a code change is moved to the quarantine suite within a day, with a ticket to fix it.

memories.title: Build test data with factory functions, not shared fixture files
memories.content: Each test creates the records it needs through small factory functions with sensible defaults instead of loading shared fixture files.

memories.title: New modules need at least 80% line coverage
memories.content: A newly added module comes with tests that cover at least 80 percent of its lines.

memories.title: Integration tests run against a real Postgres in a container, not mocks
memories.content: Tests of code that talks to the database start a real Postgres in a container; mocking the database is not accepted for these tests.

memories.title: Avoid snapshot tests for logic; assert the values that matter
memories.content: Logic is tested with explicit assertions on the values that matter; snapshot files are kept for rendered output only.

memories.title: Use property-based tests for parsers and serializers
memories.content: Parsers and serializers get property-based tests that generate many inputs and check that a round trip returns the original.

memories.title: Format on save with the project's formatter; no manual style fixes
memories.content: Editors run the project's own formatter whenever a file is saved; style is never adjusted by hand or debated in review.

memories.title: Every repository has a Makefile with build, test and lint targets
memories.content: Each repository offers make build, make test and make lint so any contributor can run them without reading scripts.

memories.title: Run local services through docker compose, not installed on the host
memories.content: Databases, queues and caches for local development run from the repository's docker compose file; none is installed directly on the laptop.

memories.title: Shell scripts start with set -euo pipefail
memories.content: Every Bash script begins with set -euo pipefail so an error, an unset variable or a failed pipe stage stops it.

memories.title: Pin the Node version in .nvmrc
memories.content: Node projects pin their runtime version in an .nvmrc file at the repository root.

memories.title: CI caches dependency downloads keyed on the lockfile hash
memories.content: Continuous integration caches downloaded dependencies under a key made from the lockfile's hash, so a changed lockfile refreshes the cache.

memories.title: Keep secrets in the password manager and inject them as environment variables; never commit them
memories.content: API tokens, keys and passwords live in the team password manager and reach programs as environment variables; none is ever committed to a repository.

memories.title: Use ripgrep instead of grep for code search
memories.content: Search code with rg, which respects ignore files and is faster than grep on large trees.

memories.title: Answer in plain sentences; bullet lists only when asked
memories.content: Replies are written as plain sentences and short paragraphs; lists appear only when the user asks for them.

memories.title: Write commit messages and documentation in British English
memories.content: Commit messages, comments and documentation use British spelling: colour, organise, behaviour.

memories.title: Skip pleasantries and get to the point
memories.content: Leave out greetings, thanks and filler phrases; start with the answer.

memories.title: Ask one clarifying question at a time
memories.content: When something is unclear, ask a single question and wait for the answer before asking the next.

memories.title: Give time estimates as ranges, never single numbers
memories.content: State how long work will take as a range, such as two to four days, with the main uncertainty named.

memories.title: No emoji in code, commit messages or documentation
memories.content: Emoji never appear in source code, commit messages or written documentation.

memories.title: Learn Rust well enough to contribute to the compiler by spring 2027
memories.content: The user aims to learn Rust well enough to land a contribution to the Rust compiler by spring 2027.

memories.title: The user works from Lisbon (UTC+0 in winter, UTC+1 in summer)
memories.content: The user is based in Lisbon and keeps Western European hours.

memories.title: The user's laptop is an ARM Mac, so build scripts must support arm64
memories.content: The user develops on an Apple Silicon laptop; scripts and container images need an arm64 variant.

memories.title: New services use PostgreSQL rather than MySQL (decided March 2026)
memories.content: In March 2026 the user chose PostgreSQL for every new service because of its JSON support and the team's experience with it.

memories.title: Use dark colour schemes in generated diagrams
memories.content: Diagrams the agent produces use a dark background with light lines and labels.

memories.title: Never send customer data to external AI services
memories.content: Customer records, names and payment details must not be pasted into or uploaded to any external AI service.

memories.title: The ledger rounds currency with banker's rounding
memories.content: Amounts in the ledger service are rounded half to even (banker's rounding), matching the accounting team's spreadsheets.

memories.title: Run ./scripts/migrate up before running the ledger's tests
memories.content: A fresh checkout of the ledger has an empty schema: run ./scripts/migrate up once before the tests, or they fail on missing tables.

memories.title: Ledger amounts are integers in minor units, never floats
memories.content: Every amount in the ledger is an integer count of cents (minor units); floating point is never used for money in this repository.

memories.title: The ledger's CI needs the LEDGER_DB_URL secret
memories.content: Continuous integration for the ledger reads the database address from the LEDGER_DB_URL secret; a job without it fails at startup.

memories.title: Ledger releases are cut from release/x.y branches
memories.content: A ledger version is prepared on a release/x.y branch made from main, tagged there, and only fixes land on that branch afterwards.

memories.title: Ledger integration tests use the testcontainers module, not a shared database
memories.content: In the ledger, each integration test suite starts its own database through the testcontainers module instead of using the shared development database.

memories.title: The website deploys from main through Netlify
memories.content: Every push to main of the website is built and deployed by Netlify.

memories.title: Website images go in public/img, compressed with squoosh
memories.content: Images for the website are compressed with squoosh and stored under public/img.

memories.title: Website copy is reviewed by marketing before publishing
memories.content: Text changes on the website wait for the marketing team's review before they are published.
